title: Weekly cut sequencer: canary gating + AI-assisted changelog & autotagging
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: Our current weekly cut and RC workflow requires manual orchestration for canary gating and release-note synthesis. This causes variability in cut times, inconsistent changelogs, and extra follow-up work from PM/Docs to assemble high-quality release notes.

Goal: Implement a 'cut sequencer' pipeline that performs: 1) deterministic RC autotagging based on branch/commit heuristics; 2) staged canary gates (smoke -> canary small traffic -> ramp) with automated health checks and rollback hooks; 3) AI-assisted changelog generation (consolidate PR descriptions, conventional commits, notable user-facing changes) and attach generated notes to the RC tag and release artifact.

Proposal overview:
- Add a new CI job (ci/cut-sequencer) triggered by the weekly-cut pipeline. The sequencer orchestrates tag creation (v{semver}+rc.{week}), builds release artifacts, and kicks canary rollout jobs.
- RC tagging policy: For weekly builds use semver patch bump, tag pattern "v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}-rc.{YYYYMMDD}.{N}". This keeps tags monotonic and traceable to cut date. When cutting an LTS window, append ".lts" (e.g., v1.20.3-rc.20250212.1.lts).
- Canary gating rules: three phases with automated checks: smoke (unit/integration quick suite), canary-1 (5% traffic, latency P95 < baseline*1.25, error-rate < 0.5%), canary-2 (30% traffic, latency P95 < baseline*1.15, error-rate < 0.25%). Failures automatically create a rollback PR and post a notification to #release-alerts and the cut-sequencer run.
- Changelog generation: run a two-step pipeline: conventional-commit parser (filter by scope=public-api,console,runtime) then AI summarizer that creates high-level bullets and user-facing examples. The pipeline will attach the generated markdown to the GH release and to the release notes S3 bucket. We will provide a manual override UI in the Console for PM/Docs to edit before publish.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Weekly+Cut+Sequencer+Spec
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1549
- Cut sequencer job: .github/workflows/cut-sequencer.yml (CI name: ci/cut-sequencer)
- Runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/release-cut-sequencer

Engineering constraints & non-goals:
- The sequencer will not change the underlying build artifact format.
- It will not fully automate cross-region promotion in this phase; we will add region promotion in Phase 2.

Why different from previous tickets: This ticket integrates AI-assisted changelog generation and a stricter phased canary with automated rollback. Existing items focused on cut cadence and RC promotion, but did not address synthesizing notes or a deterministic rc tag naming tied to cut date with LTS suffix behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1) ci/cut-sequencer job exists and can create an RC tag following the naming policy; 2) Cut job can run a smoke and two-stage canary with automated health checks; 3) Failure in any gating stage triggers an automated rollback PR and posts to #release-alerts; 4) Generated changelog is attached to the GH release and stored in the release S3 location; 5) PM/Docs can edit generated notes before marking release as 'published' in Console; 6) End-to-end test run documented in runbook and executed successfully in staging (proof: ci run ID & link).
rollout_plan: Phase A (staging): wire up sequencer to staging branch, run 3 weekly dry-runs with no public promotion. Phase B (canary opt-in): enable sequencer for internal teams; route 5% traffic for canary-1. Phase C (default weekly): enable full gating and changelog publish, add automated notifications. Each phase gated by postmortem-free runs and metric stability for 3 runs. If at any point canary fails, sequencer will revert to previous stable tag and create incident to #release-oncall.
monitoring_and_metrics: Dashboards: Release sequencer dashboard in Grafana (panel: sequencer_runs, last_run_status, canary_latency_p95_delta, canary_error_rate, rollback_count). Alert thresholds: canary_error_rate > 0.5% for canary-1 or > 0.25% for canary-2 -> Pager to Release Oncall. Acceptance metric: average cut completion time <= 25 minutes for successful runs. Track changelog acceptance rate (percent of auto-generated notes edited by PM) as quality signal.
test_plan: Unit tests for tag naming, integration tests for canary gating (use traffic replay tool on staging), e2e dry-runs that validate artifact upload, changelog generation, and GH release attachment. Coordinate with QA to run fuzzed load tests during canary windows. Required smoke job: ci/smoke-release (runs in <10m). Record run IDs in the ticket comments.
notes: Decisions: use date-based rc suffix to avoid ambiguous rc counters across parallel weekly channels. Trade-offs: AI summarizer may produce noisy microcopy — we require PM review before publish to mitigate. We will start with conservative canary percentages and tighten thresholds after 4 weeks of telemetry. Future: add automated regional promotion and LTS backport automation.
